subject.title: TUI: Support Shift+Enter for newline (Enter to send)

question: Should this TUI issue finish as docs/help coverage for the existing dependency-backed newline behavior, or should OpenClaw add a public configurable TUI send/newline keybinding surface?
rationale: Current main and the latest release have partial dependency-backed newline insertion, but configurable Enter/Ctrl+Enter/Shift+Enter behavior would add config or CLI surface that repository policy treats as product and compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Document Existing Behavior First
options.body: Update TUI docs and /help for the existing newline shortcuts, terminal limitations, and fallback behavior while deferring configurable keybindings.

options.title: Add Configurable TUI Keybindings
options.body: Introduce a maintainer-approved TUI config or CLI bridge into pi-tui keybindings with default-compatible behavior, docs, and focused tests.

options.title: Close As Dependency-Satisfied
options.body: Treat dependency-provided newline insertion as sufficient and intentionally decline the docs/help/config follow-up for this issue.

recommendation.title: Document Existing Behavior First
recommendation.body: Update TUI docs and /help for the existing newline shortcuts, terminal limitations, and fallback behavior while deferring configurable keybindings.

likelyOwner.reason: They already framed this exact remaining product choice in the issue and have the strongest TUI/docs ownership trail.
